definitions.explanation: A feeling of active ill will or opposition toward someone or something.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{目|め}には{明|あき}らかな{敵意|てきい}があった。
examples.english: There was clear hostility in his eyes.

examples.japanese: {理由|りゆう}もなく{敵意|てきい}を{向|む}けられて、{困惑|こんわく}した。
examples.english: I was bewildered by the hostility directed at me for no reason.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal noun used to describe interpersonal tension or international relations. Often appears in news and literature.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {敵意|てきい}を{持|も}つ (to harbor hostility)
- {敵意|てきい}を{向|む}ける (to direct hostility at)
- {敵意|てきい}を{感|かん}じる (to sense hostility)
- {敵意|てきい}{剥|む}き{出|だ}し (openly hostile)
